titleEn: Into the Box, a Square of Sunshine!

pages.text: "Everything out today!" Lulu tipped over the whole box. Pinecones poured out. Wooden dolls and a cloth ball rolled everywhere. Taking them out was fun. Putting them back never crossed Lulu's mind.
"Ow!" Lulu landed on the bottom after stepping barefoot on a pinecone. The cloth ball rolled away.
The favorite wooden bird was missing too. Lulu lifted the blanket and reached a forepaw under the bed. Nothing! Ears drooped, eyes brimming.
Mom pushed both wooden shutters wide. A square of sunshine fell on the attic floor. Lulu looked up.
But toys filled the square. Pinecones hid it, then dolls. "Oh? The square is all broken." Lulu tilted the head.
Mom dropped one pinecone into the box. Plop! Sunshine returned to that spot. "Into the box, a square of sunshine!"
Lulu copied, pinecones together, dolls together. The cousins came up from the yard to help. "Into the box, a square of sunshine!"
In went the last cloth ball! A whole, neat square of sunshine lay on the floor. Lulu's blue bell jingled.
Then the wooden bird peeked from the box bottom. "My bird!" Lulu hugged it. "One, same things together! Two, into the box! Three, the whole sunshine square!"
Mom hugged Lulu and the cousins together. Tidy up, and lost things appear too. "Into the box, a square of sunshine! Now the bird need not hide!"
